Core requirement: every Website and Amazon product's Customer Acquisition Cost against its break-even ceiling. CAC here is Marketing/Advertising spend ÷ Units (a spend-efficiency proxy, since no distinct order/customer count exists in source) — this is NOT the same as ROAS and is never used interchangeably with it. Break-even CAC is the maximum spend per unit that keeps CM2 ≥ 0, holding other costs fixed. 30-Day Opportunity = Daily ₹ Saved at Breakeven × 30 — the run-rate upside (or, where CAC Headroom is positive, the run-rate headroom) from moving every SKU to its break-even CAC; a modelled ceiling, not a forecast.

Apr–Jun refresh — what the data says, prioritised by ₹ impact
• FirstCry is the healthiest channel: EBITDA -1.4% (only channel near breakeven), CM2 34.4%, with zero marketing spend — commission-funded placement is working.
• Overall CM2 improved sharply on the richer dataset: 5.1% of revenue vs 1.8% in the prior refresh — underlying unit economics are healthier than previously visible.
• Gross margin is strong and stable across every channel (73–82%), confirming the cost problem is downstream of GM — marketing and overhead absorption, not product cost — for most of the business.
• 81 SKUs are flagged Green–SCALE across all channels; the best (see Product Rankings, Top 20 by EBITDA) are concentrated in Amazon Finger Paint and Combo packs.
• Website is the most broken channel on a marketing basis: EBITDA -70.5%, marketing 90.3% of revenue — spend is roughly double what CM1 can support on most SKUs.
• Blinkit is EBITDA -91.0% on just 7 SKUs — 6 of 7 are CM2-negative; only Organic Beeswax Crayons (zero marketing spend) is profitable.
• Amazon carries 60.8% of revenue but is EBITDA-negative — CM2 is healthy (20.5%) so this is an overhead-absorption problem, not a marketing problem; see Matrix 1.
• Digital Print is structurally unviable at current volume: EBITDA -1452.0% on just 62 units — overhead allocation swamps a near-zero revenue base.
• Several products sold on both FirstCry and Website show 100+ percentage-point CM2% gaps in FirstCry's favour for the identical SKU — see Channel Matrices, Matrix 3.

Refresh Summary — what changed vs the prior board report

This report covers the SAME Apr–Jun period as the previous board report — not a new quarter (Website units tie to the rupee: 3,065 in both). It is a methodology and data-quality refresh, built from a richer raw extract:

• New fields now available and used throughout: Sessions, Conversion%, DRR, and CAC/break-even columns for Website and Amazon — the CAC & DRR Analysis and Marketing Priority Score are new capabilities this refresh, not in the prior report.

• Amazon now reports FBA and FBM as separate rows for many SKUs, each with genuinely different fee structures — this raised Amazon's counted units from 9,728 to 11,334 (+16.5%) this refresh; a granularity gain from fuller data, not a comparability break.

• A formula error was found and corrected in the source file's own Amazon break-even/CAC columns (they mathematically reduced to CM2, not a break-even ceiling) — this workbook recomputes Amazon's Break-even CAC independently as CM1 − Business Support − E-vitamin.
• 5 new analytical sheets not in the prior report: CAC & DRR Analysis, Shipping Economics, Marketing Investment Matrix, Scenario Analysis, Profit Improvement Opportunities.
• Every DQ-excluded row, source-side error cell, and methodology choice is documented in the Data Quality Log — nothing was silently dropped or invented.
